title: I'm building a life sim with AI coding agents. Game Log #2 shows the game and the rough edges.
author: alexid95
selftext:
I'm Alexander, the solo developer of SimGoodie. I've been building it in my free time for a couple of months. The ambition is the character depth I loved in The Sims 2 with an open world inspired by The Sims 3. It's still an early build.

On the development side I use Claude Code alongside other coding agents. I break work into OpenSpec changes, give agents scoped implementation tasks, and have changes reviewed separately. There is also a headless simulation lab for running gameplay scenarios over simulated days. I'm trying to check whether systems work together, not just whether each change compiles.

The new Game Log gets into a very concrete example: a floor could look fully covered while still providing no walkable surface. The build previews, finished geometry and simulation all have to agree. The video also leaves in the grid mismatch, second-floor trouble and blocked interactions, so you can see where the game actually stands.

Game Log #2, with screenshots and the video: https://simgoodie.com/devlog/the-house-needs-a-floor-before-it-needs-a-reputation

Direct video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nCwWcxdxWsM

For others using agents on games with connected systems, what has helped you catch regressions between building, navigation and character simulation? That's the part I'm most interested in getting better at.
